chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the Day of Sacrifice would shave his head, clip his nails, trim his moustache, and trim the sides of his beard.
ai.seo_question: What grooming rituals did the Prophet perform on the Day of Sacrifice?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of comprehensive grooming (Taharah) performed by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) on the Day of Sacrifice, linking physical cleanliness with spiritual renewal. In Shia jurisprudence, this practice is often cited to support the recommendation of trimming the mustache and shortening the beard as part of the Fitrah, emphasizing that ritual purity extends beyond ablution to include personal appearance. The narration underscores the holistic nature of Islamic worship, where external grooming reflects internal devotion during significant occasions like Eid al-Adha.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> shaved off his<sup>saww</sup> head on the day of the sacrifice, and he clipped his<sup>saww</sup> nails, and he<sup>saww</sup> took (trimmed) from his<sup>saww</sup> moustache, and from the sides of his<sup>saww</sup> beard’.
en.sarwar: 3. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, on the day of al-Nahr (slaughtering the offering, 10th of Dhu al-Hajjah) shaved his head, cut his finger nails, trimmed his mustache and the sides (edges) of his beard.’”
